newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK RPI to edge lower in September.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK RPI to edge lower in September.

text.p: UK September retail price data are likely to show a slight decline in headline inflation but no change in the underlying measure, which excludes mortgage interest payments, economists said on Tuesday.
The Reuters consensus forecast is for headline RPI to rise 0.4 percent month-on-month, with the annual rate falling to 2.0 percent from 2.1 percent.
Underlying annual inflation (RPIX) is seen flat at 2.8 percent year-on-year. If forecasts prove correct, RPIX will have stuck stubbornly at that level for five consecutive months.
The figures will be released at 0830 GMT on Thursday.
Economists said a number of contrary factors would influence retail prices and warned the data may not be as favourable as is usual for September.
On the one hand, lower seasonal food prices and the resumption of supermarket price wars, coupled with lower mortgage rates will help nudge inflation down.

Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets, estimated the mortgage rate cuts that followed June's official rate cut would take 0.06 percent off the overall index with falling seasonal food prices taking 0.1 percent off the headline rate.
"Also, we are hopeful September could be the month when core inflation finally starts to respond to the steep drop in core producer output price inflation over the last year," he said.
But working in the opposite direction are rising petrol prices and the risk that retailers are taking advantage of the recent upswing in consumer activity.

"Normally, September shouldn't be too bad," said Schroder economist David Philpotts. "But it will be interesting to see how much retailers have hiked prices on clothing and footwear...following the increase in consumer demand."
Economists said if there was to be any further improvement in inflation in the current cycle, it would come in the next few months or not at all.
"If there's no improvement now, I can't see any coming through next year...when the input price cycle will be turning up again, commodity prices will start to rise," Philpotts said.
Economists also warned it was touch and go as to whether the Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke would meet his target of 2.5-percent underlying inflation by year-end.

"(The headline rate) will probably be just above 2.5 percent by the turn of the year, but you'd have to be quite optimistic to say it will be below there and stay below there. Given the recent pick-up in consumer sales, the risks are on the upside," Philpotts said.

With jittery UK gilts anticipating benign inflation data, economists said a headline rate safely close to two percent in September coupled with Monday's weak manufacturing data would be enough to limit any losses.
They added the data would probably reinforce the growing view a pre-emptive rise in UK interest rates would be desirable for the markets and a pre-election cut negative.
"There's almost a perverse situation where they could react badly to a rate cut and perhaps react favourably to a rate rise," Philpotts said.
